title: You have a second brain in your gut
hook: YOUR GUT IS A SECOND BRAIN
voiceover: You have a second brain. It's in your gut, and it has over 500 million neurons. Scientists call it the enteric nervous system, and it can operate completely on its own, without a signal from your actual brain. It controls digestion. But it also makes 90 percent of your body's serotonin — the chemical that controls your mood. So when you get a gut feeling? That's not a metaphor. That's literally a second brain talking to you. The next time your stomach feels off before a big decision, it might know something you don't. Follow Mindbloom for one fact a day.
